title: The hypertrophy series: understanding sandbagging to promote qualitative sets
summary: NH defines sandbagging as doing less than you could in a set without a good reason, usually forced by rep schemes like 10x10, 5x5 or 3x5. Intentional sandbagging is useful in warm-ups and as one rep in reserve on strength work. Back-off work should go to failure. Late-session sets in irrelevant intensity windows become a form of sandbagging even at failure.
claims: Sandbagging is not giving 100% within a set, leaving intensity and quality tonnage on the table with no logical reason
Bad rep schemes like 10x10 force sandbagging, because you cannot complete them if you push early sets hard
NH is not a fan of 5x5 or 3x5 because they force sandbagging
If set 1 of a 5x5 were a true 5RM, set 2 would be 4 or 3 reps, then 3 or 2, and so on
Sandbagging is fine when you choose it for a reason, but bad when the rep scheme forces it and wastes tonnage quality
Warm-ups are deliberate sandbagging: you stop well short because extra reps would be a waste
On strength work, sandbag by one rep, the danger rep, for injury prevention and form quality
If you can get 6 reps on the first strength set, take 5 so the next set can still get 4 instead of 3 or bad-form reps
After strength work, eliminate sandbagging and take every set to failure since loads are no longer maximal
After bench strength work, do close-grip bench 3x6-10 to failure every set
Late in a session, sets taken to failure can still be sandbagging because the loads are irrelevant compared to your strength work
Sandbagging belongs at the start and, involuntarily, the end of the session but should not happen in the middle
5x5 and 3x5 are bad as strength work but acceptable as a complementary accessory after strength work, where static tonnage accumulation is their role
Strength work reps should go down from set to set as muscular endurance drops, which 5x5 fails to allow
A 5x5 still yields 25 reps and 3x5 15 reps of quality volume, progressing slowly themselves but carrying over to the main lift
A 5x5 used as the day's only strength lift with nothing for it to carry over to is worthless
